Certerra is a growing national provider of testing, inspection, and certification services that support innovation in new product development, quality assurance, for project delivery, and engineered solutions for asset management. We are passionate about contributing to the sustainable development of the communities we serve. We are a national firm with a global reach serving national and international clients from 30+ offices located in 10 states and are ranked on ENR’s Top 500 list alongside the nation’s top firms. With a 60-year history, Certerra has a passion for high-end services, constant innovation, and investment in the development of world-class laboratory facilities, and interactive management technologies. Each member of our staff is committed to service, innovation, and the success of our clients.

Certerra is a nationally recognized provider of engineering, testing, inspection, and certification services supporting innovation, quality assurance, and resilient infrastructure. With over 1,800 professionals nationwide, we combine technical expertise with practical field knowledge to ensure the communities we serve are built to last.

Help Build Our South Puget Sound Geotechnical Team

Certerra is growing our Tacoma office and laboratory, strategically located to serve South Puget Sound and some of the region's largest and most technically challenging infrastructure, military, federal, transportation, and civil construction projects.

We're looking for an experienced geotechnical professional – geologist, engineering geologist, geological engineer, geotechnical engineer, or similarly qualified professional – to become a key member of this growing team.

Washington LG or PE licensure is highly desirable, but we also encourage highly qualified candidates who are eligible for or actively progressing toward professional licensure to apply.

Our South Puget Sound team supports a diverse and growing portfolio of work, including military and federal projects at Naval Base Kitsap and other regional installations, Sound Transit and transportation programs, major civil infrastructure, dams and water resources, commercial development, and other complex construction throughout Western Washington.

This is a hands-on technical role spanning both design-phase geotechnical investigations and construction-phase support, with a strong emphasis on evaluating and documenting actual soil and rock conditions encountered during construction.

We're looking for someone with approximately five or more years of relevant experience who is comfortable moving between the field and office, exercising professional judgment, working directly with construction teams, and turning field observations into clear technical documentation and recommendations.

Environmental experience is also highly desirable and provides an opportunity to help expand our capabilities in the South Puget Sound market.

Duties

The successful candidate will work across geotechnical design, field investigation, and construction, with a significant portion of the role focused on construction-phase geotechnical services.

Typical Responsibilities May Include

Provide geotechnical and engineering geology support during major civil, military, federal, transportation, and infrastructure construction
Observe, evaluate, and document soil and rock conditions encountered during excavation and construction
Confirm field conditions relative to design assumptions, plans, specifications, and geotechnical recommendations
Perform detailed soil and rock logging, mapping, and conditions documentation
Observe and document foundation excavations, bearing conditions, slopes, excavations, and other geotechnically significant construction activities
Observe and document rock and soil anchor systems, including drilling and installation
Document drilling conditions, materials encountered, depths, groundwater, refusals, and other relevant subsurface conditions
Identify and communicate differing or unexpected field conditions to engineers, contractors, owners, and project teams
Support geotechnical instrumentation and monitoring activities, including settlement, groundwater, vibration, and other monitoring programs
Plan and perform subsurface investigations, including drilling, test pits, sampling, and field exploration
Review field and laboratory data and develop or support geotechnical recommendations
Support foundation, earthwork, site development, and geologic hazard evaluations
Prepare field memoranda, technical reports, recommendations, proposals, and other project documentation
Provide technical direction and mentoring to geotechnical technicians and junior field personnel
Support groundwater and environmental investigations based on experience
Assist with project management, client coordination, budgets, schedules, and technical deliverables

This combination of design, construction, environmental, and monitoring work reflects the broader geotechnical professional role identified for Certerra Northwest, including subsurface investigations, geologic hazard assessments, foundation recommendations, earthwork evaluations, construction support, instrumentation and monitoring, groundwater evaluations, and environmental investigations.

Education/Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Geology, Engineering Geology, Geological Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, or a related field
Approximately five or more years of relevant professional experience
Washington Licensed Geologist (LG) or Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
Demonstrated experience with both design-phase geotechnical investigations and construction-phase geotechnical support
Strong soil and rock identification, logging, evaluation, and documentation skills
Experience evaluating actual field conditions and communicating technically significant findings to project teams
Experience with excavations, foundations, earthwork, drilling, anchors, or other heavy civil construction activities
Ability to interpret geotechnical reports, construction plans, specifications, and other technical documents
Strong technical writing and communication skills
Ability to exercise sound professional judgment in active construction environments
Ability to communicate effectively with engineers, contractors, owners, technicians, and other project stakeholders
Ability to independently manage field assignments and technical responsibilities
Valid driver's license and ability to travel to project sites throughout South Puget Sound and Western Washington
Ability to meet access, background, and identity verification requirements associated with certain military and federal project sites

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas are particularly encouraged to apply:

Washington Licensed Geologist (LG) or Professional Engineer (PE)
Candidates eligible for or actively pursuing Washington LG or PE licensure are also strongly encouraged to apply
Engineering geology or geotechnical consulting
Military and federal projects
Heavy civil, dam, transportation, or major infrastructure construction
Construction-phase geotechnical observation and conditions documentation
Rock and soil anchor installation observation and documentation
Instrumentation and monitoring
Groundwater investigations
Environmental site investigations, assessments, or environmental consulting
Project management and client-facing responsibilities
Mentoring or directing geotechnical field personnel

Certerra Northwest's current recruiting profile similarly identifies LG and PE credentials, environmental experience, and instrumentation and monitoring experience as desirable qualifications for its geotechnical professionals.

Be Part of What's Next in South Puget Sound

This is an opportunity to join a growing Tacoma operation at an exciting time.

You'll have the opportunity to work on major military and federal facilities, transportation programs, dams and water resources, and complex infrastructure projects throughout South Puget Sound and Western Washington, while helping grow Certerra's geotechnical capabilities in the region.

We're looking for someone who enjoys being where the work is happening—evaluating conditions, solving problems, documenting what is actually encountered in the field, and helping project teams make sound technical decisions during construction.

At the same time, you'll have opportunities to contribute to design-phase investigations, environmental work, project management, client development, and the continued growth of our Tacoma geotechnical team.
